# AiEngineered

> AiEngineered builds instant quote calculators for trades, clinics, salons and other local businesses in the UK, Ireland and the US. Customers pick a job, see a guide price for the area, and send their details to the business by email. Price: £197 setup, then £49 a month, cancel any time. Run by Liam Hockley, a sole trader in the United Kingdom.

## How it works
- A business builds a free preview with its name, town and type of business.
- If they like it, they pay £197 setup plus £49 a month through Stripe and receive their calculator link and website code by email within minutes.
- Their customers choose a job and size, see a guide price range, and send a request. The request is emailed to the business with one-tap call and WhatsApp buttons.
- Clinics, salons and similar businesses edit their own prices from a private link; trades tell AiEngineered what they charge and the price level is adjusted to match.
- Cancelling is self-serve through Stripe; the plan runs to the end of the paid month, then requests stop.

## Guides
- [Should you show prices on your website?](https://aiengineered.co.uk/guides/should-you-show-prices-on-your-website/): Usually yes, as a guide range rather than a fixed price. It answers the first question most customers have, filters out people whose budget doesn’t fit, and you still confirm the final price.
- [How to add a quote calculator to your website, Instagram and Google profile](https://aiengineered.co.uk/guides/add-a-quote-calculator-to-your-website/): Paste one line of embed code into your website builder’s HTML or embed block, or share the calculator as a link in your Instagram bio, Facebook page and Google Business Profile. No website? The link works on its own.
- [Quote calculator or contact form: which gets you better enquiries?](https://aiengineered.co.uk/guides/quote-calculator-vs-contact-form/): A contact form asks customers to wait for a price; a quote calculator shows a guide price first and sends you the job, size and budget with the enquiry. Calculators suit businesses whose customers ask “how much?” first; contact forms suit work that can’t be priced without a conversation.
